title: Look up — the cross, and where London starts
learning_goal: Know the forecourt cross is an 1865 replica and that London's distances are measured from the Charles I statue.

narration.script: Look up. The cross is a replica, put up in 1865: twenty-one metres — seventy feet — of Portland stone. The original of 1291 stood a couple of hundred metres off to your right. King Charles the First rides there now, in bronze. London's distances are still measured from him, not from this cross.

variants.clear: Look up. This cross is a copy, put up in 1865: twenty-one metres — seventy feet — of stone. The original, from 1291, stood a little way to your right. A statue of King Charles the First rides there now. London still measures its distances from that statue, not from this cross.
